title: Test beads no-db mode

Investigate permission aggregation duplication - DRY violation
description:
## Problem
Permission aggregation logic is duplicated in 3+ locations:
- `AccountProfileHandler.AssignRole()`
- `AccountProfileHandler.RemoveRole()`  
- `PermissionService.GetUserPermissionsAsync()`

## Evidence from Red Team Analysis
Permissions exist in THREE places:
1. `Permission` components
2. `Role.PermissionIds[]` arrays
3. `SecurityProfile.PermissionIds[]` denormalized

## Risk
- DRY violation makes bugs likely
- No single source of truth for permission calculation
- Inconsistent permission state possible if one location missed

## Investigation Needed
1. Map all locations where permission aggregation occurs
2. Identify canonical source of truth
3. Design `PermissionAggregator` service or similar
4. Determine if denormalization is necessary or if caching is sufficient
close_reason: Permission duplication eliminated - PermissionIds removed from SecurityProfile, DRY violations fixed, 24 new security tests added

title: Investigate query system 'fetch all' pattern - scaling alternatives
description:
## Problem
EntityQuery uses in-memory set operations that don't scale:
```csharp
var allRoles = await DataContext.Query()
    .WithAll<Role>(r => true)  // Loads EVERYTHING
    .ToEntityComponents();
// Then filters in C#
```

## Evidence from Red Team Analysis
This pattern appears in:
- `AccountProfileHandler` - loads all roles
- `RegistrationSystem` - loads all accounts  
- `AuthHandler` - various fetch-all patterns

## How It Actually Works
1. Three separate DB queries for entity IDs
2. Load all IDs into memory
3. Set intersection/union in C#
4. Fetch components for surviving IDs

## Risks
- O(n) memory for n entities
- No database query planning
- No index usage across component types

## Alternatives to Investigate
1. **Expression translation** - Convert LINQ to SQL WHERE clauses
2. **PostgreSQL CTEs** - Use WITH queries for set operations
3. **Materialized views** - Pre-compute common joins
4. **Document pattern** - When is direct SQL appropriate?
5. **GraphQL path** - Push complex queries to GraphQL layer
close_reason: COMPLETE: Filter<T> type-safe query API implemented - replaces deceptive LINQ-like lambdas with explicit operators

title: [jarvis-12.5] SECURITY: Penetration test permission boundaries
description:
## Objective
Verify permission system cannot be bypassed or escalated.

## Attack Vectors to Test

### 1. Privilege Escalation
- [ ] User cannot add roles to their own profile
- [ ] User cannot modify Role.PermissionIds
- [ ] User cannot access other users' SecurityProfiles
- [ ] Admin role removal actually revokes access

### 2. Cache Poisoning
- [ ] Cached permissions cannot outlive role removal
- [ ] Cache key cannot be guessed/forged
- [ ] Invalidation is synchronous (no window of access)

### 3. Race Conditions
- [ ] Concurrent role add/remove doesn't grant extra permissions
- [ ] Permission check during cache invalidation is safe

### 4. Input Validation
- [ ] Invalid role IDs are rejected
- [ ] Malformed permission strings are rejected
- [ ] SQL injection in permission checks

### 5. Authorization Bypass
- [ ] Cannot access protected endpoints without valid permission
- [ ] Cannot forge permission headers
- [ ] RLS actually blocks cross-tenant access

## Deliverable
Security test report: `docs/security/permission-pentest-report.md`

## Exit Criteria
All attack vectors tested and documented. Zero bypasses found.
close_reason: Security and E2E tests created - 24 new tests, all pass

title: [jarvis-12.6] VALIDATE: E2E permission flow integration test
description:
## Objective
Prove the complete permission flow works end-to-end.

## Test Scenario
```
1. Create Permission: { Resource: 'patients', Actions: ['read', 'write'] }
2. Create Role: { Name: 'Doctor', PermissionIds: [permissionId] }
3. Create User with SecurityProfile: { RoleIds: [roleId] }
4. Authenticate user → get JWT
5. Call protected endpoint /api/patients → should succeed
6. Remove role from user
7. Call protected endpoint /api/patients → should fail (403)
8. Verify cache was invalidated
9. Re-add role
10. Call protected endpoint → should succeed again
```

## Implementation
Create new test file: `core.jarvis.api.tests/Integration/PermissionE2ETests.cs`

## Exit Criteria
E2E test passes reliably (run 10 times, no flakes).
close_reason: Security and E2E tests created - 24 new tests, all pass

title: E2E: Integration tests proving Filter<T> works end-to-end
description:
Comprehensive integration tests proving the solution works:

## Test 1: Case-Insensitive Email Lookup
- Create account with email 'Test@Example.COM'
- Query with Filter<Account>.Eq(a => a.Email, 'test@example.com').IgnoreCase()
- Assert: Finds the account

## Test 2: Exact Match
- Create role with name 'admin'
- Query with Filter<Role>.Eq(r => r.Name, 'admin')
- Assert: Finds exactly one role
- Query with Filter<Role>.Eq(r => r.Name, 'Admin') (case sensitive)
- Assert: Finds nothing (proves case sensitivity)

## Test 3: Comparison Operators
- Create orders with amounts 50, 100, 150
- Query with Filter<Order>.Gt(o => o.Amount, 75)
- Assert: Returns orders with 100 and 150

## Test 4: String Contains
- Create items with names 'Apple Pie', 'Apple Sauce', 'Banana'
- Query with Filter<Item>.Contains(i => i.Name, 'Apple')
- Assert: Returns 2 items

## Test 5: Combined Filters (And)
- Create users with various statuses and roles
- Query with Filter<User>.Eq(u => u.Status, 'active').And(Filter<User>.Eq(u => u.Role, 'admin'))
- Assert: Returns only active admins

## Test 6: Combined Filters (Or)
- Query with Filter<User>.Eq(u => u.Status, 'active').Or(Filter<User>.Eq(u => u.Status, 'pending'))
- Assert: Returns active and pending users

## Test 7: In Operator
- Query with Filter<Role>.In(r => r.Name, new[] { 'admin', 'user', 'guest' })
- Assert: Returns all matching roles

## Test 8: All() Operator
- Query with Filter<Role>.All()
- Assert: Returns all roles (explicit fetch-all)

## Test 9: Performance Baseline
- Create 1000 test accounts
- Time: Filter<Account>.Eq(a => a.Email, 'test@test.com')
- Assert: Query executes in < 100ms (uses index)
- Assert: Memory usage is O(1) not O(n)

## Test 10: SQL Injection Prevention
- Query with Filter<Account>.Eq(a => a.Email, "'; DROP TABLE accounts; --")
- Assert: Query executes safely, returns no results
- Assert: Table still exists

THESE TESTS ARE THE PROOF OF LIFE. If they pass, the solution works.

Permission cache has no automatic invalidation on changes
description: PermissionService.cs caches SecurityProfile with 5-min TTL but invalidation is incomplete. Missing invalidation: (1) UpdateProfile() doesn't invalidate, (2) Role permission changes (GrantPermission/RevokePermission) don't invalidate user caches, (3) Direct DB commits bypass handlers. Users can operate with stale permissions for up to 5 minutes after role changes.

title: Lazy service resolution in DataContext complicates debugging
description: DataContext.cs uses 6 Lazy<T> services to avoid circular dependencies. Issues: (1) Deferred init obscures real dependency problems, (2) Two services wrap already-injected params unnecessarily, (3) Stack traces include Lazy framework noise, (4) Root cause is circular dependencies - should refactor to smaller interfaces instead of masking with lazy loading.
